Subject: Connectivity bounceback: private-link deployment causing intermittent TCP resets

Hi Sam / GFH Netops team,

We're seeing intermittent TCP resets and a small number of failed uploads after you cut over the private link yesterday evening. Symptoms reported by your app team: 2–3% of POSTs to /v1/ingest are failing with RST, large transfers stall and then retry.

What we've observed so far (attached):
- gfh_private_link_topology.png — your topology and our expected flow
- initial packet capture (attached) with a few sessions showing RSTs

Immediate asks:
1) Can you confirm MTU on your side of the VXLAN/private-link? We often see MSS/MTU discrepancies cause mid-stream resets once path MTU discovery fails.
2) Any recent firewall or load‑balancer changes on GFH edge in the 22:00–23:30 UTC window?
3) If possible, please provide router logs for the same time window and a pcap of a failing session.

We'll triage from our side too — I've looped in Karthik (network infra) and Vanessa (customer success) so we can coordinate an escalation if needed. If you prefer a maintenance window to flip configs, propose a time and we'll be ready.

Thanks,
Alex Martinez

Redwood Inference

Subject: Re: Connectivity bounceback: private-link deployment causing intermittent TCP resets

Thanks Sam — that frag-needed + DF pattern plus subsequent RST is exactly what I'd expect for an MTU/MSS mismatch combined with NAT resizing the packet. Two hypotheses:

1) Path MTU on GFH -> Redwood path is 1400 (some middlebox doing 1400) but GFH host is sending 1500 payloads with DF set; the ICMP gets back but either gets dropped/filtered or the DF causes resets when reassembly fails.
2) SNAT on the GFH border is rewriting outer headers and changing packet size such that the firewall/rewrite device on-path enforces a smaller MTU on the post‑SNAT packet.

Quick checks we can run (I can run #1–#2 from our side if you can coordinate timing):
- On a test host behind your border: curl --limit-rate to reproduce and tcpdump on your border + our front-door, compare MSS values.
- Provide output of conntrack/session table counts around failure. If SNAT session expiry/reuse is triggering abnormal path behaviour, we might see session churn.

Redwood data we can provide:
- I can run a targeted pcap from our front-door to correlate sequence numbers once you share a failing client IP/time.

For preservation and escalation: I opened JIRA SUP-7421 and uploaded the GFH pcap and our initial topology. I recommend we do the proposed maintenance window 02:00–04:00 UTC (tomorrow) to:
- temporarily enable MSS clamp on your border to 1360 and observe client success rate
- if MSS clamp fixes it, plan a longer-term fix (MTU path audit / reconfigure intermediate device)

If GFH wants us to try a quick mitigation from our side first (MSS clamp on our edge), we can do that inside a 10-minute window and roll back. Let me know preference and I'll coordinate with on-call.

Karthik
Sr. Network Engineer — Redwood Inference

Immediate mitigation plan (proposed):
- 08:15 UTC: Redwood to enable MSS clamp 1360 on front-door for a 15-minute test (quick rollback plan in place).
- 08:30 UTC: GFH to enable MSS clamp 1360 on their border for comparison (if they can).
- If both reduce failure rate, plan a path MTU audit and update network diagram.

Communications: Alex — please send the short customer-facing note to GFH product ops after the 08:15 test with results. Karthik — you'll own the test run and rollback. On-call infra, please confirm readiness to flip and roll back within the time box.
